hints: Notice the word hot, as chlorine reacts very differently with cold versus hot sodium hydroxide.
Recall the hot disproportionation equation: 3 moles of $\text{Cl}_2$ produce only 1 mole of $\text{NaClO}_3$.
Convert your moles of chlorate to mass using $m = n \times M_r$ with $M_r$ of $\text{NaClO}_3$ about 106.5.
walkthrough:
**Recall the correct hot reaction**

Chlorine disproportionates, and temperature decides the product. With hot concentrated $\text{NaOH}$, chlorate(V) forms.

$$3\text{Cl}_2 + 6\text{NaOH} \rightarrow 5\text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Use the 3 to 1 mole ratio**

From the equation, 3 mol of $\text{Cl}_2$ make 1 mol of $\text{NaClO}_3$. So divide by 3.

$$n(\text{NaClO}_3) = \frac{0.600}{3} = 0.200 \text{ mol}$$

**Convert moles to mass**

Now find $M_r$ of $\text{NaClO}_3$ and multiply by moles.

$$M_r = 23.0 + 35.5 + (3 \times 16.0) = 106.5 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$$
$$m = 0.200 \times 106.5 = 21.3 \text{ g}$$

options.A: Correct. 0.600 mol of Cl2 gives 0.200 mol of NaClO3 by the 3:1 ratio, and 0.200 x 106.5 = 21.3 g. Well done for using the hot equation.
options.B: Incorrect. This is the mass of NaClO from the cold reaction. Cold NaOH gives 1 mol NaClO per 1 mol Cl2, so 0.600 x 74.5 = 44.7 g. The question states hot, so chlorate, NaClO3, forms instead.
options.C: Incorrect. This assumes a 1:1 ratio of Cl2 to NaClO3 (0.600 x 106.5 = 63.9 g). It forgets the balanced equation needs 3 Cl2 for every 1 NaClO3.
options.D: Incorrect. This is roughly double the correct mass and comes from inverting the ratio, as if 1 mol Cl2 makes 2 mol NaClO3. Check the equation again, 3 Cl2 makes only 1 NaClO3.
